Customer success and renewals · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Account expansion signals

Nicolas · Account Growth Analyst

Of the 340 client schools of an education platform, 22% use more students than the contract licenses, 14% above on average, and the contract provides for an annual adjustment with a 5% tolerance.

When it runs
On the 1st of every month, after the number of active students and teachers per school is consolidated, and immediately when a school requests more than 10% new student accounts in a single week
What it delivers in production
A monthly queue of expansion signals per school, with evidence, estimated annual value and a suggested approach, approved by the renewals manager; each approved signal becomes an opportunity in the CRM with a deadline for the conversation.
Who decides
Flags; the manager approves the approach
Effort
Calibrate on 12 months; 3 months of queue
Set up5 steps · 8 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

# Expansion signal rules and price table

## Price table (annual)
| Item | Price |
|---|---|
| Student in a new segment or new unit, elementary | R$ 290 |
| Student in a new segment or new unit, high school | R$ 320 |
| Student in a new segment or new unit, early childhood | R$ 250 |
| Assessments module, per school | R$ 9,600 |
| Reports module, per school | R$ 6,000 |
Overage uses the extra_student_price of the school's contract.

## Signal rules
- Valid students = active_students minus test_accounts. Teachers never count.
- OVERAGE: valid students above licensed x (1 + tolerance) in the reference month and in the previous one. February and March do not generate overage. Value: valid students of the reference month minus that limit, times the contract price.
- UNCONTRACTED SEGMENT: valid students in the month in a segment outside the contract, times the segment price.
- MODULE REQUESTED: 3 or more tickets for the same uncontracted module in the 90 days up to the end of the reference month. MODULE IN TRIAL: teachers_using_pct of 50 or more. Value by the table.
- NEW UNIT: school in units.csv registered in the 60 days up to the end of the month, with no contract. Value: valid students times the segment price.
- Public school operator: NOT APPLICABLE, REFER TO LEGAL, out of the total.

## Rules with no leeway
- Reference month of this test: October 2026 (previous: September). Ticket window: Aug 2 to Oct 31, 2026; units window: Sep 1 to Oct 31, 2026.
- Test accounts come out before comparing. E.g.: E103 has 445 active and 30 test accounts, 415 valid, below 420: no signal. E104 with teachers would give 328, but the students are 302, below 304.5: no signal.
- One month alone is not enough. E.g.: E102 exceeds 525 only in October: no signal.
- Overage math. E.g.: E101 has 350 valid, limit 315: 35 x R$ 290 = R$ 10,150.
- A module already contracted does not become a signal. E.g.: the 3 reports tickets of E103.
- Escalations apply together and the highest one wins. E.g.: E101, E107 and E111 belong to operator M7, with 3 flagged schools: the sales director leads with M7, even with manager-level values.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

A signal is a proposal, and an overage charge never reaches the school on the employee's initiative: the approach belongs to the renewals manager, because the adjustment clause lives alongside a relationship the school can end at renewal. Schools run by a public school system leave the commercial queue and go to legal, since the amendment follows its own procedure. Teacher, coordination and test accounts do not count as overage students. February and March do not generate overage signals, because enrollment is still settling.

Common mistakes

  • Counting teacher, coordination and demo accounts as overage students and taking to the school a number it can dispute in a minute.
  • Including transferred or inactive students who were never deactivated on the platform in the number of active students.
  • Proposing an additional module to a school whose adoption of the module already contracted is below 40%; there, the right approach is adoption, not a sale.
  • Flagging overage at the enrollment peak of February and March, before the base settles, and burning the signal's credibility with the manager.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Expansions formalized per yearfrom 5 to 25 to 40 in the first year of operationestimate based on the described routine
Closed expansions that were flagged 60 days or more earlier80% or more, with fewer than 30% of signals discardedestimate based on the described routine
Additional annual revenue billed from overagefrom close to zero to the range of 3% to 5% of the base's revenueestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Expansion signals, consolidation of 2026-08-31, 340 schools analyzed, 27 signals.

School 118 (private group, 300 licensed students in elementary, 5% tolerance) | SIGNAL: overage | 352 active students in July and 361 in August (20% above, 2 months in a row) | estimated value: 46 additional students x R$ 290 = R$ 13,340/year | approach: contractual adjustment provided in clause 4, present it as a regularization before the December renewal
School 275 (private, elementary-only contract) | SIGNAL: segment not contracted | 6 high school classes active since 2026-08-10 | estimated value: 180 students x R$ 320 = R$ 57,600/year | approach: meeting with the principal in September, before the usage becomes a habit with no contract
School 091 (private) | SIGNAL: module requested through support | 4 tickets asking for the assessments module in 60 days (ids 7710, 7742, 7801, 7855) | estimated value: R$ 9,600/year | approach: offer a 30-day trial to the coordinator who opened the tickets
School 160 (public school system, licensed through an administrative contract) | SIGNAL: 11% overage | estimated value not applicable | approach: FORWARD TO LEGAL, an amendment depends on the public contract procedure

SUMMARY: estimated annual value in approvable signals R$ 412 thousand; 3 schools with a signal discarded in March because enrollment was still settling, re-evaluated now.
